abstract.para: &sbd; configuration is complex, involving many interrelated settings and timeouts. Even though &crmsh; helps to keep these settings aligned, upgrades or manual changes can sometimes introduce misconfigurations. The crm sbd configure show and crm sbd status commands automatically check the &sbd; configuration and list any issues. You can also check the configuration directly using the crm cluster health sbd command. This command lists issues with the &sbd; resource agent, configuration files, timeout settings, and more. It can also fix some of these issues automatically.

important.title: Cluster restart might be required
important.para: Some fixes, such as timeout changes, require restarting the cluster services. The &sbd; health script checks whether a cluster restart is required and whether it is safe to do so automatically. If any non-fence resources are running, the script warns you to restart the cluster services manually. This allows you to put the cluster into maintenance mode first to avoid resource downtime. However, be aware that the resources won't have cluster protection while in maintenance mode.

step.para: Log in either as the &rootuser; user or as a user with sudo privileges.

The output shows a list of warnings for any issues and reports the status of the &sbd; timeout configuration (either OK or FAIL). If &crmsh; can fix any issues automatically, you'll also see the following output:

step.para: Run the &sbd; health check with the --fix option to automatically fix issues:

Some fixes, such as timeout changes, require restarting the cluster services. The script checks whether a cluster restart is required and whether it is safe to do so automatically. If any non-fence resources are running, the script warns you to restart the cluster services manually.
Run the &sbd; health check again. If there are still issues but the output doesn't include the --fix suggestion, you must fix these issues manually.
